data.body:
Fixes bug Bebc6fe14a1: ddflow/core/globs.py:114 overlap only treats * and ? as wildcards when taking the literal prefix; '[' is literal. Probe: overlap('src/[ab]x.py','src/ax*') and the reverse both return False although src/ax.py matches both (prefixes 'src/[ab]x.py' and 'src/ax' neither startswith the other; fnmatch of either pattern against the other fails). Two claims can therefore be granted on files they both write. Other class cases (src/[ab]*.py vs src/a*.py) are caught by luck of fnmatch. Fix: cut the prefix at the first of * ? [ and add a regression table with class cases.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bebc6fe14a1 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bebc6fe14a1 --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug Bebc6fe14a1: globs.overlap misses a character-class glob against a literal-prefix glob (src/[ab]x.py vs src/ax*)

evidence.note: Claim: overlap('src/[ab]x.py','src/ax*') returns False even though both match src/ax.py (same for src/bx*), so two claims can be granted on one file. Falsifier: the probe returns False on unfixed code. Probe (worktree): python3 -c "from ddflow.core import globs; print(globs.overlap('src/[ab]x.py','src/ax*'))" -> False. Verdict CONFIRMED. Regression test test_overlap_cuts_the_prefix_at_a_character_class fails on the unfixed tree (assert False) and passes after the fix.

Read the work-queue rules (AGENTS.md) and the two recalled rules that govern the item from : r-task-phase-needs-wave (task names phase/deps/wave) and r-gemini-key-load (export GEMINI_API_KEY before reviews). None adds a constraint the fix violates: the fix is a bug-fix task, and its regression test is declared via the tests/test_globs.py glob. Committed fix + test together.

ddflow/core/globs.py overlap() now cuts the literal prefix at the first of * ? [ (new _literal_prefix helper), so a character class is treated as a wildcard boundary. Added regression test test_overlap_cuts_the_prefix_at_a_character_class in tests/test_globs.py. tests/test_globs.py: 50 passed; test_glob_update_overlap.py + test_lease_reacquire_overlap.py: 19 passed. Commit 068249f64.

chunk_findings.detail: The new prefix check now treats a shared prefix before `[` as sufficient for overlap, but character classes can be disjoint. For example, `globs.overlap("src/[!a]x.py", "src/ax*")` now returns True because `_literal_prefix` yields `"src/"` and `"src/ax"`, and `"src/ax".startswith("src/")` is True. However no file can match both patterns: the first requires the character after `src/` to be anything but `a`, while the second requires it to be `a`. The old code returned False for this non-overlapping pair.

chunk_findings.detail: `_literal_prefix` treats every `[` as a wildcard, so disjoint character classes at the same position now collapse to the same prefix. For example, `globs.overlap("src/[ab]x.py", "src/[cd]x.py")` returns `True` because both prefixes become `"src/"`, yet no file can match both patterns (`[ab]` vs `[cd]` are disjoint and both require `x.py`). The previous code returned `False` for this pair. The added test only asserts positive cases, so it will not catch this over-broad classification and the function reports an impossible common file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/globs.py:_literal_prefix

chunk_findings.detail: `_literal_prefix` returns `""` when the pattern starts with `[`, and `overlap` treats an empty prefix as a universal match (`if not pa or not pb: return True`, the bare-`*` branch). Given `overlap("[ab].py", "zzz.py")` both the old and new `fnmatch` checks fail, then `pa == ""`, so the function returns True. That is wrong: `[ab].py` matches only `a.py` and `b.py`, and neither matches `zzz.py`. The same input was False before this change (`pa` stayed `"[ab].py"`). The new comment only justifies a shorter prefix on the `startswith` check; it does not make a leading character class cover every path.

data.probe: Over-reporting is the safe direction: overlap() documents that it only decides whether to re-order, and a disjoint-class false positive (src/[ab]x.py vs src/[cd]x.py -> True) merely serializes two claims, never grants two claims on one file. The bug Bebc6fe14a1 is the DANGEROUS direction (false negative: src/[ab]x.py vs src/ax* read False though src/ax.py matches both), which is now fixed. test_globs.py: 50 passed.

data.probe: Same over-approximation as #1: the character class is read as a wildcard boundary, so two DISJOINT classes at the same position now collapse to one shared literal prefix and read as overlapping. chunk_findings.detail: `_literal_prefix` returns `""` when the pattern starts with `[`, and `overlap` treats an empty prefix as a universal match (`if not pa or not pb: return True`, the bare-`*` branch). Given `overlap("[ab].py", "zzz.py")` both the old and new `fnmatch` checks fail, then `pa == ""`, so the function returns True. That is wrong: `[ab].py` matches only `a.py` and `b.py`, and neither matches `zzz.py`. The same input was False before this change (`pa` stayed `"[ab].py"`). The new comment only justifies a shorter prefix on the `startswith` check; it does not make a leading character class cover every path.

chunk_findings.detail: The new one-empty-prefix branch creates false negatives for leading single-character wildcards. Given `globs.overlap("?.py", "a*.py")`, both `fnmatch` checks are false because each treats the other's wildcard as a literal, `_literal_prefix("?.py") == ""` and `_literal_prefix("a*.py") == "a"`, so the new final expression `(not pa and a.startswith("*")) or (not pb and b.startswith("*"))` returns `False`. But both globs match `a.py`, so the conflict detector misses an overlap and two claims can be granted on the same file. The same false negative affects the intended class case at the root, e.g. `globs.overlap("[ab]x.py", "ax*")` returns `False` while both match `ax.py`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/globs.py:overlap

chunk_findings.detail: The new empty-prefix branch only treats a leading `*` as overlapping, so a leading `?` or `[` now returns False whenever `fnmatch` of the two pattern strings fails. That misses real intersections: `overlap("[ab]x.py", "ax*")` and `overlap("?x.py", "ax*")` both return False, yet `ax.py` matches both patterns (same miss as Bebc6fe14a1, only with the class or `?` at the start). The comment is wrong that `fnmatch` already answered those cases — neither pattern string matches the other, so the prefix check is the only remaining gate and it now denies the overlap.

Given `overlap("[ab].py", "zzz.py")` both the old and new `fnmatch` checks fail, then `pa == ""`, so the function returns True. That is wrong: `[ab].py` matches only `a.py` and `b.py`, and neither matches `zzz.py`. The same input was False before this change (`pa` stayed `"[ab].py"`). chunk_findings.detail: The new empty-prefix branch creates a false negative for a leading character class or leading `?` when the real overlap goes through the other pattern’s wildcard. For example, `overlap("[ab].py", "a*.py")` should be `True`: both patterns match `a.py`. The two `fnmatch` checks fail because `fnmatch("[ab].py", "a*.py")` treats `[ab].py` as a literal name, and `fnmatch("a*.py", "[ab].py")` treats `a*.py` as a literal name. Then `_literal_prefix("[ab].py") == ""` and `_literal_prefix("a*.py") == "a"`, so line 146 returns `False` because the empty-prefix pattern does not start with `*`. This is the dangerous false-negative direction the change is meant to prevent; the comment’s claim that such sharing was already answered by the `fnmatch` checks is false.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/globs.py:146

chunk_findings.detail: The new empty-prefix branch returns True only when the empty side starts with `*`. That is a false negative for leading `?` or `[`, which `fnmatch` of either pattern text against the other does not catch. Given `overlap("a[bc]", "?[bc]")`, both `fnmatch` checks fail (`a` vs `?`, `[bc]` vs `[`), `pa` is `"a"` and `pb` is `""`, and the function returns False, yet `ab` matches both. The same miss hits `overlap("[abc].py", "[cde].py")` (shared file `c.py`): both prefixes are empty, neither pattern starts with `*`, result False. Before this change those pairs returned True. A false negative is the direction that grants two claims on one file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/globs.py:146

data.probe: Confirmed: the empty-prefix branch in the refinement returned False for leading ? and [ab] classes when the real overlap goes through the other pattern's wildcard ([ab].py vs a*.py both match a.py). Fixed in commit a931be1b1: a leading wildcard (any of * ? [) is now read as unanchored -- an empty literal prefix assumes overlap, so the answer errs toward True (safe direction), never False. Pinned test asserts [abc].py overlaps [cde].py (shared c.py). test_globs.py: 50 passed.
